lesson.meaning: To finish doing something, or to make something whole and ready.
examples: Please complete your registration process by the end of the day.
The team needs to complete this project before the deadline.
Have you completed all the necessary steps for the new software installation?
We can only move forward once we complete the initial review.
I feel so good when I complete all my tasks for the day.
lesson.memory_tip: Think of 'complete' as finishing a task or making something whole and ready. It means 'done'!
